title: Shift resume, scrub & follow-ups — APAC night -> EU morning
content:
Context / TL;DR:
- APAC night shift observed a short-duration tokenization queue spike at ~2026-03-12T23:18Z impacting hosted-api (region: ap-southeast1). Error budget effect: transient 0.6% error increase for 7m. No customer-facing SLA breaches reported but two partner customers saw increased tail latency and filed alerts via PagerDuty.

What I (APAC night) saw / timeline (concise):
- 2026-03-12T23:12Z: Degraded tail latency alerts (SRE-3421) fired for route /v1/generate (p95 -> p99).
- 2026-03-12T23:15Z: Autoscaler reacted, added a small burst pool instance but warmup lagged; tokenization queue grew.
- 2026-03-12T23:18Z: Several requests hitting model variant quantized-x failed with 502s due to worker OOMs on worker-7 (short spikes).
- 2026-03-12T23:19Z: Automated fallback to non-quantized variant succeeded for ~85% of traffic; remaining hits retried by client causing transient spikes.
- 2026-03-12T23:25Z: Ops mitigations applied (soft throttling route + adjust batching_window to 10ms).
- 2026-03-12T23:30Z: Metrics stabilized, tokenization queue drained by 23:36Z.

Immediate mitigations taken (by night shift):
- Enabled automatic fallback policy to non-quantized model for the affected customer tag (rule id fb-qp-2026-03).
- Applied a temporary soft rate limit (10% reduction) for heavy routes from the partner orgs that reported alerts.
- Reduced batching_window from 25ms -> 10ms for the affected pool to reduce head-of-line latency and queue accumulation.
- Opened a follow-up incident ticket and paged Platform SRE for kernel/driver trace (ticket: SRE-3421).

Root-cause hypotheses (initial):
- Worker OOMs likely caused by a combination of input sequence-length spike (many >8k token requests) and a quantized kernel regression introduced in PR #1284 (platform inference optimizer).
- Autoscaler warmup delay made burst instances not available fast enough; warmup thresholds are still conservative for quantized variant cold-starts.
- KV-cache invalidation race: several requests attempted to rebuild KV caches concurrently (notes in Confluence link), increasing peak memory temporarily.

Evidence collected / logs & traces (quick links):
- Kernel-side oom dumps: s3://prod-logs/oom/2026-03-12/worker-7-oom-2318.log
- APM trace sample: trace-id: tr-A9f3 (attached to SRE-3421)
- Metric snapshots: grafana/dashboard?k=tokenization-queue&ts=2026-03-12T23:10..23:40
- Partner alert PD: PD-6781 (partner A)

Customer impact summary:
- Partner A: observed tail-latency spikes and 6 of their requests returned 502s during 23:18-23:23Z (they retried, causing amplified load).
- No billing anomalies detected.
- No data plane confidentiality incidents.

Immediate follow-ups (must-do within 24h):
- (Owner: Marco Chen) Reproduce high-seq workload in staging with quantized-x kernel + PR #1284 merge commit. Estimate: 4h to validate reproducibility.
- (Owner: Evan Liao) Add temporary heuristic: if worker memory usage >85% and many >4k sequences are in-flight, prefer non-quantized fallback earlier. Implement as runtime configuration: depoyment window: 6h for canary.
- (Owner: Aisha Patel) Update on-call runbook section "quantized-variant-fallback" with clearer activation thresholds and rollback steps. Draft completed, needs review (link: PR to runbook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/72).
- (Owner: Team) Add targeted telemetry: per-pool sequence-length distribution histogram (already instrumented? -> confirm).

Runbook draft changes proposed (short patch):
- New step: when p99 latency increases >150% for >3m and worker oom_count > 1 in the same pool, trigger immediate automatic fallback to compatible model variant AND pause new warmups for that variant for 10m.
- Add an explicit step to check for concurrent KV-cache rebuild events: query "kv_rebuild_count" over the last 5m, if >3, escalate to platform.
- Add guidance: apply soft route-throttle (-10%) instead of full route disable for partner orgs unless >0.5% error budget consumed.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is PR #1284 the proximate cause or just a catalyst for a latent memory pressure bug? (Marco)
- Can we tighten autoscaler warmup thresholds for quantized models without harming steady-state cost? (SRE infra team)
- Why did worker-7 experience an OOM while other workers in the same pool did not? Node-level hardware flakiness or kernel scheduling variance? (Needs deeper postmortem traces)

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Repro script + staging run (Marco) — ETA: 2026-03-13 16:00Z.
- Runtime fallback heuristic PR (Evan) — ETA: 2026-03-13 22:00Z.
- Runbook patch (Aisha) — draft PR out, review requested by 2026-03-14 09:00Z.
- Add sequence-length histograms to dashboards (Observability) — ticket OBS-907, ETA 2026-03-15.
- Postmortem draft (owner: on-call lead during incident) — initial skeleton by 2026-03-16.

Handoff checklist for incoming EU morning shift:
- Read this doc + SRE-3421 + PR #1284.
- Verify that the temporary soft throttle is still in place for the two partner orgs (route config).
- Confirm that the fallback policy fb-qp-2026-03 is enabled and has not been re-disabled by auto-heal.
- Re-check worker-7's node status and kernel OOM traces; ensure agent logs rotated and archived.
- If reproducer exists in staging, validate canary and monitor memory pressure for 30m post-merge.

Notes to incoming shift (free-form):
- If you see a recurrence but without OOMs, lean on the KV-cache hypothesis: many long sequences can cause simultaneous cache inflation and increase transient memory. Avoid immediate model variant toggles unless OOM evidence exists.
- Partner teams may run aggressive client-side retries; coordinate with Partner Success to ask them to backoff if we need to run live tests.
- Keep an eye on p99-p999 latency (the tail) rather than p50 which is stable.

Short-term risk assessment:
- Likelihood of recurrence in next 72h: medium (because quantized kernel change + warmup conservatism).
- Customer-visible impact if repeated: low-to-medium (tail latency spikes, a small percentage of 502s).

Document versioning / provenance:
- Author: Aisha Patel (APAC night, on-call)
- Edits: Marco Chen (repro notes), Evan Liao (runtime heuristics)
- Runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/72

Appendix (quick commands):
- Query recent OOMs: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.prod/ops/ooms?since=2026-03-12T23:00Z
- Toggle fallback (admin): ./ctl route fallback enable fb-qp-2026-03 --org partnerA --duration 600
- Dashboard snapshot: grafana/dashboard?s=tokenization-queue&from=2026-03-12T23:10&to=2026-03-12T23:40

End of handoff. Incoming EU shift: please ack this doc and add any new observations as separate bullet entries under the top of this doc (date-stamped).
